content.thinking: I should strip the revision name out of the root_cause field.

action_items.item: Once PR #319 is merged, deploy a revision carrying its scrape.yaml change to io-shop and confirm that samples arrive again.
Check the other services that took the estate-wide `<protocol>[-<purpose>]` port rename for scrape configurations that still ask for a port by its old name.
Route MetricsAbsent on io-shop to on-call so that it pages a person.

causal_chain.step: Nobody using the shop was seen to notice anything wrong. What was seen instead: io-shop's metrics stopped arriving after the minute at {T5.2}, and MetricsAbsent fired at {alert_raised}.

No samples were collected because the ServiceMonitor that ran at c3c36da picks the endpoint to scrape by the port name `metrics` (S1). At that same revision, the metrics port is named `http-metrics` (S2). No port matched the name the scrape asked for. S1's own comment says the operator does not treat that as an error: it just leaves an empty target list.

ruled_out.what: The earlier deploy of revision 2c8f731 (P1): samples kept arriving with it in place until the minute at {T5.2}, and D1 shows the port rename came in c3c36da, not in the revision P1 deployed.
A feature-flag change: the flag provider showed {T16.2} flag changes by anyone but Argus in the {T16.3} hour before {T16.4}.

causal_chain.step: The port had a new name because revision c3c36da, deployed at {P2.1}, renamed every port to the estate-wide `<protocol>[-<purpose>]` convention, including metrics -> http-metrics. It changed only deploy/values-production.yaml and did not touch deploy/scrape.yaml (D1). All {T13.2} replicas were running that revision as of {T13.1}.

input.cause_in_plain_words: A configuration change renamed the connection that the monitoring system collects the shop's measurements from, but the monitoring setup still looked for the old name, so it found nothing to collect.

contributing_factors.factor: No check was seen that the port name the scrape asks for matches `metrics.portName`. S1's comment says nothing checks that the two agree, and that a name matching no port is not an error.
contributing_factors.had_it_been_otherwise: Renaming the metrics port without updating scrape.yaml would have failed before deploy, and the metrics would never have stopped.

contributing_factors.factor: MetricsAbsent on io-shop paged nobody: no on-call incident was linked to the alert.
contributing_factors.had_it_been_otherwise: A person would have been engaged when the alert fired, ready to take up the draft fix and restore metric collection sooner.

went_well: Argus refused to roll back c3c36da, because the only action that would test the leading candidate would undo a rename made on purpose (T18). It moved to a forward fix instead.
The Code-Fix Agent opened draft PR #319 {T20.1 - alert_raised} after the alert. The PR proposes pointing the scrape at `http-metrics` and adding a test that keeps the two names in step.

input.root_cause: The platform's Prometheus ServiceMonitor (deploy/scrape.yaml) picks the shop's metrics endpoint by port name and still asks for `metrics`. The change renamed that port to `http-metrics` in deploy/values-production.yaml and left scrape.yaml as it was. The selector then matched no port, and by the file's own comment the operator treats a name that matches no port as an empty target list, not an error, so no samples were collected.
input.still_at_risk: The scrape still asks for a port name that no port has, so any real trouble in the shop would go unseen by metric-based alerts, and because nothing checks that the two names agree, a later rename on either side could cut off the metrics again.
input.symptom: Nobody using the shop was seen to notice anything wrong; instead, the shop's metrics stopped arriving.
